subject: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up: Acme Health (HIPAA)
message_1_subject: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up: Acme Health (HIPAA)
message_1_body:
Thanks again for the time today — quick recap and a few follow-ups so we can size Dedicated for you.

Summary of what I heard:
- Deployment preference: Dedicated capacity (HIPAA / data residency in US).
- Primary workload: clinical summarization + patient Q&A inside Acme’s portal. No PHI is retained by Redwood; logs must be auditable.
- Expected traffic: planning for a pilot with bursty spikes, then steady growth. Need to confirm peak concurrency and average request size.

Questions / asks:
1) Can you confirm peak concurrent requests we should plan for (concurrent open sessions)?
2) What's the average and 95th-percentile token mix per request (prompt tokens + completion tokens)?
3) Any hard latency SLOs for p50/p95? (e.g., p95 < 250ms for short prompts, or is 500–1,000ms acceptable)
4) Any preference on GPU family (we can recommend H100 vs A100 based on model and quantization)?

Next steps I propose: Rafael (SE) will send a ballpark sizing with 2–3 options (conservative / recommended / cost-optimized). I’ll also attach a draft mutual action plan and a preliminary quote for Dedicated so you can share with procurement.

Attachments: draft MOP + preliminary quote (attached).

Thanks — Marissa

message_2_subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up: Acme Health (HIPAA)
message_2_body:
Thanks Marissa — high level answers below so Rafael can size: 

- We do want Dedicated (HIPAA) and US-only residency.
- Pilot targets: peak concurrency ~40 concurrent sessions (we define a session as an active web user/request).
- Peak RPS (requests per second): ~25–35 at pilot peak; production expected to double in 6–9 months.
- Token mix: average prompt ~= 800 tokens, average completion ~= 200 tokens, so ~1,000 tokens/request typical. 95th percentile could be up to 2,000 tokens for some long clinical notes.
- Latency SLO: for patient-facing quick Q&A, p95 ideally < 800ms. For longer summarization jobs we can accept up to 2s.
- Model: we are open to your recommendation; we value response quality but also need predictable latency and cost.

Also important: procurement wants clear cost-per-hour and a clause on burst autoscaling (how much and how fast). Can you include burst strategy and alternate model fallbacks for budget control?

Thanks — Samir
Samir Patel | Head of Product, Acme Health
samir@acmehealth.com | (650) 555-0147
message_3_subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up: Acme Health (HIPAA)
message_3_body:
Appreciate the detail, Samir — helpful. Ballpark sizing and options below (very high level; we’ll bench with your workload to refine):

Notes on assumptions:
- Tokens/request: avg 1,000 tokens, 95th 2,000 tokens.
- Target peak ~35 RPS (requests/sec) sustained bursts to 60 RPS for short windows; peak concurrency ~40 active streams.
- Model choice: recommendation is to run the pilot on a high-quality open decoder model tuned for instruction (we can discuss exact model family). For best throughput/latency we recommend quantized FP16/INT8 variants where applicable.

Sizing options (estimate):
1) Recommended (performance + cost balance): 4 x H100 (80GB) nodes in Dedicated pool. Rationale: H100 gives best latency for long-context workloads and supports larger batch sizes for improved token/sec. Provides headroom for peaks and supports quantized versions.
2) Conservative/high-performance: 6 x H100 (for lower p95 and more headroom at peak bursts).
3) Cost-optimized: 6–8 x A100 (80GB) nodes — slightly higher latency on the longest requests but lower hourly cost depending on region.

Autoscaling / burst behavior:
- We can configure a baseline Dedicated pool (the nodes above) plus burst capacity that draws on spare capacity in the cluster for short windows. Typical burst policy: allow +50% capacity for up to 10 minutes, with automated fallback to cheaper model variants if cost exceeds thresholds.

Estimated throughput guidance (very approximate):
- With 4 x H100 and quantized model, expect to comfortably handle ~25–40 RPS at ~1k tokens with p95 in the 400–900ms range depending on batch config and exact model.
- With 6 x H100, headroom up to ~60 RPS with improved p95.

What we need from you to refine:
- A representative sample of 50–100 requests (anonymized) showing token distributions and typical prompt templates.
- Preferred model quality vs cost tradeoff (e.g., prefer lower latency + fallback to smaller model vs prioritize single-model consistency).
- Confirmation that the autoscale burst policy above is acceptable, or specific limits procurement requires.

I’ll schedule a short perf-readout / sizing call if you want Rafael + infra folks to walk through numbers. Happy to run a short pilot benchmark on our side with a redacted sample.

--
Rafael Mendes | Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rafael@redwood.com | +1 (212) 555-0220
